text: The circumstance, that forks were not invented in ancient times, gave occasion to the use of napkins at meals to wipe the fingers; also when the meal was finished, and even before it commenced, an apparatus was carried around for washing the hands. The boy or slave who poured out the water, also held the napkin or towel for wiping the hands dry. The word mappa, said to be of Carthaginian origin, denoted a smaller kind of napkin, or a handkerchief, which the guests carried with them to the table. The mantele, as it was larger than the mappa, was sometimes used as a table-cloth.
